chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'For the place of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), there is a known sanctity; whoever recognizes it and seeks refuge by it is granted refuge.' I said, 'Describe its place to me.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Measure out from the place of his grave today, twenty-five cubits from its front, and twenty-five cubits by his head, and twenty-five cubits from around his legs, and twenty-five cubits from behind him.'

And the place of his grave from the day he was buried is a Garden from the Gardens of Paradise, and from it is an ascending stairway from which the deeds of his visitors ascend to the sky, and there is none from an Angel, nor a Prophet in the skies, except that they are asking Allah to permit them regarding the performance of Ziyarah of the grave of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). So a multitude descends and a multitude ascends.

key_terms.زِيَارَة: Pilgrimage or visitation (specifically to the grave)

ai.seo_question: What are the dimensions and spiritual significance of the grave of Imam Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi outlines the specific geographical boundaries of the sanctified zone around Imam Al-Husayn’s grave, establishing it as a 'garden of Paradise' where the spiritual merit of visitors ascends to the heavens. It underscores the unique cosmological status of the grave, noting that Prophets and Angels alike seek divine permission to visit, reflecting the Shia belief in the intercessory and spiritual centrality of the Ahl al-Bayt.
